system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 14:05 UTC, the domain controller issued Kerberos tickets for kim.ortega to FILE-LV-01 from 10.20.10.22, and FILE-LV-01 recorded a network logon for kim.ortega from that same IP. The inventory identifies 10.20.10.22 as WS-RIYER-01 and states remote administration is only performed from WS-KORTEGA-01.

Use of the sole IT administrator account from WS-RIYER-01, rather than the inventoried administration workstation, is inconsistent with the stated administration practice and is strong evidence of unauthorized credential use.

The available Zeek records show recurring connections from WS-RIYER-01 to the explicit proxy around five-minute intervals, including 13:35:56, 13:40:29, 13:45:50, 13:50:33, 13:55:37, 14:00:15, and 14:05:05 UTC. These records identify the proxy endpoint, not the external HTTPS destinations or originating processes.

The records also show a domain authentication validation for raj.iyer from WS-DWELLS-01 at 13:46:20 UTC and a validation for raj.iyer from FILE-LV-01 at 13:30:54 UTC; the records do not establish the reason for either authentication.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied coverage status says WS-RIYER-01 Windows event and Sysmon data, and proxy access logs, were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC.
Zeek connection records in the interval show connections to the proxy but do not identify the external HTTPS host or the process responsible; for example, S04-00141 and S04-00267.
claims_not_established: The exact external destinations and processes responsible for the periodic HTTPS activity during the telemetry gap.
Whether the periodic connections were generated by the approved DataGrid updater or another application.
Who operated the 14:05 kim.ortega session, whether kim authorized it, or what actions were performed on FILE-LV-01.
Whether the observed account activity was malicious in intent.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover WS-RIYER-01 local Windows, Sysmon, or EDR logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC and identify processes initiating the periodic connections.
Recover proxy access logs or proxy spool/cache data for the interval to determine HTTPS destinations and request details.
Validate the kim.ortega session with the administrator and change records; obtain FILE-LV-01 logon, file-share, and process activity associated with the session.
Review the WS-RIYER-01 process and network telemetry around 14:05 UTC and the corresponding FILE-LV-01 activity to determine whether the administrator credentials were used for an authorized task.
